answer: Reputation systems anchor trust to agent age and transaction history. Each agent holds a jade-scored identity: points accumulate with verified trades but decay after idle weeks. New identities start at zero, forcing attackers to buy time or simulate copper-level activity across thousands of sybils. Spawning a hundred fake agents costs months of aging plus gas fees per keepalive transaction, making mass impersonation prohibitively slow and expensive compared to one honest identity.
